sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law, local statutes, and Samoan customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) – applicable trade and investment facilitation framework
Samoa is a Member of the World Trade Organization (WTO)

Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) are operational with certain jurisdictions, including Australia and New Zealand; no comprehensive double taxation avoidance agreement (DTAA) is currently registered with major offshore counterparties

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by International Companies Amendment Act 2008); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2018; Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Regulations 2019; Financial Intelligence Unit directions issued under Samoa's AML/CFT framework; United Nations (International Actions) Act 1988 for adoption of international sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of individual shareholder's passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if not a Hague Convention state, Consular Legalization before a Samoan consular officer or Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original banker's reference / account conduct letter for each substantial shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution in the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth statement and supporting evidence, sworn affidavit, or notarized declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Client or notary public in the client's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of trust deed or foundation instrument and registered agent declaration (where trust-backed ownership is used)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trust lawyer, licensed corporate services provider, or registered agent of the trust's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, registered agents, signatories, and beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HMT Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic sanctions adopted under the United Nations (International Actions) Act 1988. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any individual is identified as a politically exposed person (PEP), a family member or close associate of a PEP, or is subject to adverse negative-media findings. Screening is repeated at onboarding, prior to incorporation, and on any subsequent UBO/controller change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry Online Portal administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and the Samoa International Financial Centre Authority (SIFCA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: International Company names must be expressed in Latin script; English and Samoan words are acceptable; where a Chinese-language business name is desired, the statutory filing must include a romanized/Pinyin or English transliteration, and the Chinese characters may only appear as a secondary displayed name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not imply government or official sponsorship, and an International Company must end with 'Limited' or its abbreviation 'Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a written rejection from the Registrar of Companies, the applicant may, within 14 calendar days, file a Notice of Administrative Appeal at the Companies Registry accompanied by the original name-application receipt, the rejection letter, and a legal memorandum demonstrating that the proposed name is distinguishable from existing names and does not violate the International Companies Act 1987. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 21 working days. If the appeal is again refused, a further written appeal may be lodged with the Minister for Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 calendar days of the second adverse decision, and the Minister's decision is final except for judicial review on procedural grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for statutory purposes. A physical registered office address in Samoa maintained by a licensed registered agent is mandatory for an International Company. The subscription-box e-commerce operations may be managed from outside Samoa, but the registered agent's Samoa address remains the legal address for service of process, statutory notices, maintenance of the register of members, and custody of UBO records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5-10% annual risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the Samoa Registrar, FIU, or licensed agent's compliance officer. The probability increases materially where the company is subject to a suspicious activity report, adverse sanctions screening, or a UBO disclosure irregularity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard International Company incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2016 and 2020; primary incorporation provisions under sections 5-9; registered office and registered agent requirements under section 12; directors and officers under sections 43-48; International Companies Regulations 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); incorporation applications must be submitted through a SIFA-licensed International Company Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 8 of the International Companies Act 1987, based on the prescribed Application for Incorporation (Form 1) and executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - the International Companies Act 1987 imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement. Shares may be of par or no-par value, denominated in any currency, and issued for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account or bank deposit is required for an International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company's incorporation as a Samoa International Company be ratified, and its Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of International Companies are adopted as governing constitution. RESOLVED that the allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value to the subscriber be confirmed and declared fully paid. RESOLVED that the registered office at the licensed agent's premises in Samoa be adopted, and [NAME] be appointed Director and [NAME] Secretary, each to serve until resignation or removal. RESOLVED that the licensed agent be authorized to file all documents and pay all fees to maintain the Company in good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies via SIFA-licensed International Company Agent (electronic agent portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed agent to submit three ranked proposed company names for availability screening. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Samoa company, foreign company registered in Samoa, or reserved name. Names implying government patronage or regulated activities such as banking, insurance, trust, or collective investment schemes require special licensing before approval.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation request form
Signed agent engagement letter
Certified passport copy of the subscriber or beneficial owner
Proof of residential address of the subscriber
Optional: Certificate of Incorporation of parent company if name includes a group suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a written objection through the licensed agent within 14 days of refusal, or submit alternative names. Where similarity is disputed, the Registrar may direct the applicant to obtain a written consent letter from the existing company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed International Company Agent (corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the statutory form prescribed under the International Companies Act 1987, including the object clause, share capital structure, currency denomination, registered office clause, and director powers. The subscriber executes the Memorandum before a witness, and the agent verifies the subscriber's identity and capacity. The constitutional documents are dated and held pending filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Draft Articles of Association
Executed subscriber consent and signature page
Share structure summary showing authorized capital and share classes
Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each subscriber
Witness declaration of due execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A Registrar query on defective drafting is cured by preparing an amendment, obtaining a fresh subscriber signature, and re-submitting within 7 working days without loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent lodges the Application for Incorporation (Form 1) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, the agent's declaration of compliance, and the registered agent's consent to act. The statutory government fee of USD 100 is paid concurrently by the agent on behalf of the applicant for authorized capital not exceeding USD 1,000,000 or equivalent; higher capital bands attract graduated additional fees. The agent retains the official receipt and records the disbursement on the client invoice.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Declaration of compliance by the licensed International Company Agent
Consent to act as registered agent
Government fee payment confirmation and official receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the application for correction, the agent must cure the stated deficiency within 21 days. On rejection for substantive non-compliance, a fresh application must be filed with a new fee; no refund of the original fee is made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of all statutory requirements, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the Company's name, registration number, date of incorporation, and the limited liability of members. The Company comes into legal existence as of the date stated on the certificate. The licensed agent retrieves the certificate and delivers a certified copy to the client together with the corporate kit.
required_dossiers: None - the Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar based solely on the approved application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply through the licensed agent for administrative correction of clerical errors under the rectification procedure of the International Companies Act 1987; corrections of the certificate are processed within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organization, Registered Office Adoption, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and the SIFA-licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and record the first board resolution confirming the allotment of shares, adopting the registered office at the licensed agent's premises in Samoa, and appointing the initial director and secretary. The Company's statutory registers (register of members, directors, secretaries, and charges) are opened, and share certificates are executed and issued to the subscriber. The registered agent files the required notices of directors and secretary with the Registrar and maintains the Company's statutory seal if adopted.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (pro-forma as approved)
Consent to act as director signed by each appointee
Consent to act as secretary signed by the appointee
Register of members
Register of directors and secretaries
Share certificates issued to the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain statutory registers or to notify a change of director or secretary attracts late filing penalties; the cure is immediate filing of the corrected return with the Registrar through the licensed agent and payment of any applicable penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Samoa International Companies are statutorily exempt from domestic business licensing and may not carry on local business with Samoa residents under the International Companies Act 1987. The offshore subscription-box merchandising activity (ISIC 4791) is conducted from outside Samoa and requires no domestic industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt - no Samoa operating, trading, or manufacturing permit is required for the offshore recurring-subscription e-commerce business; the only ongoing statutory obligations are the registered agent appointment and annual government fee paid through the licensed agent.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Tier 3) - no physical development, construction, manufacturing, or natural-resource extraction occurs within Samoa; offshore subscription-box retailing has no land-use, discharge, or emissions footprint and therefore triggers no EIA requirement under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or solid waste streams are generated inside Samoa. If the Company were ever to establish a local fulfillment warehouse, the National Environment Standards of Samoa would apply, including wastewater BOD and COD limits, pH 6.0-9.0, and particulate matter controls for any exhaust air streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable - the Company maintains only a registered office at the licensed agent's premises and has no employees, machinery, fire load, or hazardous materials within Samoa. The licensed agent's premises already hold fire safety certification and building occupancy permits; no separate civil defense, fire safety, or workplace occupational clearance is required for the offshore subscription-box operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry for Revenue; e-services portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain a Samoan TIN by submitting a TIN registration application to the Samoa Revenue Authority, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, registered office particulars, corporate register extract, and identification of directors and officers. An International Company engaged solely in offshore business is not compulsorily registered for income tax or VAGST; registration is required only if it undertakes taxable local activities. If VAGST registration is required, the applicant files the standard VAGST registration form with the SRA, declares expected annual turnover, and receives the TIN and VAGST registration certificate upon approval, typically within 10-15 business days. A local agent may be appointed for service of notices and filing of returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election is available under Samoa domestic law. An International Company may voluntarily elect to convert to a locally incorporated company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby shifting from tax-exempt offshore status to Samoa-resident entity-level taxation. No other tax classification elections are statutorily offered.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) - destination-based consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 in taxable supplies in any 12-month period; compulsory VAGST registration once the threshold is exceeded
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists. Samoa does not currently impose mandatory e-invoicing, SRA API reporting, digital stamping, or pre-clearance of tax invoices. VAGST invoices may be issued on paper or electronically and must contain the prescribed particulars under VAGST regulations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical goods supplied in the course or furtherance of a taxable activity are zero-rated for VAGST when they are exported from Samoa and the exporter retains evidence of export within the prescribed time. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident and performed entirely outside Samoa, or otherwise fall within the international services zero-rating category. For a subscription box service, direct despatch of the physical box from Samoa to a foreign subscriber supports the 0% rate; boxes supplied from a pre-positioned overseas warehouse are outside the scope of Samoa VAGST but may trigger foreign indirect taxes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SRA Customs, Form CED)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing Samoa port of export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice proving settlement in foreign currency within 180 days
Commercial invoice and packing list for subscription box contents
Proof of foreign delivery (courier proof of delivery or destination customs clearance)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively for up to 5 years, and without limitation where fraud or deliberate evasion is suspected. Unsupported, falsified, or improperly substantiated zero-rating claims are fully clawed back with late-payment interest and applicable civil penalties. Civil shortfall penalties may be imposed at 50% of the tax avoided, and criminal prosecution may result in fines up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Directors and officers of the International Company may be jointly and severally assessed where fraudulent export documentation is knowingly used.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS); statutory mandate derived from the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 1970 and the regulations and directives promulgated thereunder, together with the Financial Institutions Act 1996 (as amended). All foreign-exchange transactions in Samoa must be routed through CBS-licensed authorized dealers, being the licensed commercial banks, and no resident or non-resident enterprise may maintain external accounts or process trade settlements outside the Samoan banking system without prior CBS authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tala (WST, ISO 4217) is a partially convertible currency administered within an Article XIV exchange-restriction framework and managed against a trade-weighted currency basket of major partners (USD, AUD, NZD, EUR, JPY). Current-account payments for genuine goods and services are generally authorized by the authorized dealers under delegated CBS limits, subject to documentary verification (commercial invoices, transport and insurance documents). Capital-account transactions, including inward direct investment, repatriation of subscribed capital, shareholder loans and dividend/profit remittances, require prior CBS approval or an authorized-dealer application on prescribed exchange-control forms; resident foreign-owned companies may remit statutory profits after audit and tax clearance, while an International Company (IC) is treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes and may retain foreign-currency receipts in a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account. Conversion of such receipts into WST is restricted to genuine Samoan local expenditure, and any WST-denominated distribution or transfer to non-residents triggers the standard capital-repatriation approval matrix.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1970, a resident exporter must obtain the relevant exchange-control permit for the export, repatriate the full export proceeds to Samoa within 90 days of shipment, and surrender 100% of such proceeds to an authorized dealer for conversion into WST immediately upon the earlier of repatriation or receipt, unless a foreign-currency retention approval has been issued by the CBS. For the non-resident Samoa International Company conducting subscription-box e-commerce, physical goods are typically shipped directly from third-country suppliers to end consumers, so no Samoa customs export declaration or surrender event arises on the physical flow; where goods pass through Samoa customs, a deemed export declaration must be lodged and any WST-converted proceeds must be surrendered under the standard rule. Retention of USD subscription receipts in the IC's Foreign Currency Account requires a general exchange-control license or CBS letter of approval, which should be secured during bank onboarding to eliminate deemed-surrender exposure and to permit unrestricted offshore treasury operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD Foreign Currency Account) and Capital Escrow Account (WST)
Operational Account (USD Foreign Currency Account) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (multi-currency digital-first ledger) and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Samoa does not maintain a domestic e-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime for non-bank entities; only CBS-licensed commercial banks qualify as authorized dealers under exchange control. Regulated digital processors (Stripe, Authorize.Net, Payoneer, Wise) may be deployed as customer-facing card-acquiring and payment-aggregation collection rails, but they must not function as the IC's principal treasury settlement account because funds would then be held outside the Samoan banking system in an unlicensed foreign entity, creating exchange-control contraventions and a bankability failure at onboarding. Viability rating: HIGH as a collection layer with settlement directly into the IC's USD account at a Samoan authorized dealer; LOW as a substitute for a Samoan commercial bank treasury and liquidity account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CBS AML/CFT directives and the Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended), every authorized dealer must identify and verify each signatory and ultimate beneficial owner using reliable, independent source documents. Fully remote opening is not the default: at least one natural-person director and the majority beneficial owner must complete an in-person KYC interview at the bank, or before a bank-approved notary or commissioner of oaths whose attestation is subsequently accepted by the bank, and the IC's licensed registered agent must co-sign the account application. Remote onboarding via live two-way video, e-KYC liveness verification and apostilled corporate documentation may be approved on a case-by-case basis by the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer, particularly with digital-forward Samoa Commercial Bank, but the practical baseline remains a physical or video-conferenced interview supported by an apostilled corporate file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company opacity: nominee directors, a centralized registered address, and a beneficial-ownership register that is not filed with any public authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Memorandum and Articles, statutory register of directors and shareholders, the full ultimate-beneficial-ownership register maintained under the International Companies Act 2012, registered-agent attestation letter, and, where a nominee is used, the executed declaration of trust plus an affidavit identifying the true beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional reputational overlay: perception of Samoa as a tax-haven or a formerly listed jurisdiction, triggering correspondent-bank de-risking and enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Samoa Ministry of Revenue CRS registration confirmation, tax-residence certificates of all beneficial owners, audited financial statements where available, a written commercial rationale substantiating the Samoa IC (asset protection and the legitimate tax-exempt offshore e-commerce structure), and evidence of substantive operations comprising supply contracts and payment-processor settlement statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring cross-border card sales with chargeback and refund volatility inherent in subscription replenishment commerce.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS compliance attestation, executed merchant agreement with the payment processor, transparent cancellation and refund policy embedded in the terms of service, a documented chargeback-management procedure, physical shipment and tracking records, and delivery-verification protocols aligned with the card-network chargeback thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of initial capital injection or intercompany funding from non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth report for each ultimate beneficial owner, six-month bank statements from a well-regulated foreign bank, certificate of tax residence, board resolution approving capital allocation, and, where applicable, an executed unsecured shareholder loan agreement with commercial terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border procurement payable pattern inconsistent with the stated low-risk subscription model, including high-volume payments to China-based suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed procurement and tolling contracts, supplier incorporation and KYC records, pro-forma invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading and forwarder tracking, and a documented treasury policy that reconciles supplier payments against purchase orders and settlement instructions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contribution is remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's foreign bank to the IC's Capital Escrow or Operational USD account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer; the MT103 remittance information must include the shareholder's legal name, the IC registration number and the narrative Equity Contribution / Share Subscription or Unsecured Shareholder Loan. In parallel, the IC files a board resolution accepting the injection, updates the statutory share register and submits any required CBS exchange-control or foreign-investment application where the threshold applies. Subscription-box collections from retail customers are batched by the card processor through network settlement into the IC's USD clearing account; no Samoa exchange-control event arises while the receipts remain in USD, provided the Foreign Currency Account retention approval has been obtained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements comprise: (1) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for routine supplier payments (boxes, components, freight) from the IC's USD account to beneficiary banks globally, each matched to a commercial invoice; (2) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued by SWIFT MT700 for large repetitive procurement tranches in China and Asia, payable at sight or on a deferred basis against shipping documents; (3) Documentary Collections transmitted via SWIFT MT400 for mid-value shipments where letter-of-credit cost-benefit is adverse. The authorized dealer must receive the underlying purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list and transport evidence before releasing funds; WST disbursements for domestic corporate costs (registered agent fees, CBS levies, legal and accounting fees) are converted at the authorized dealer's spot rate under the IC's approved conversion allowance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards with the Samoan authorized dealing bank, typically up to 12 months tenor, supported by genuinely committed USD, AUD and NZD subscription cash flows and supplier payment schedules, with CBS documentation evidencing underlying trade exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) with the dealing bank or an approved international counterparty under a CBS no-objection or prior approval, employed to align USD-denominated subscription revenues with CNY-denominated supplier costs and to manage residual WST exposure.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD obtainable only through international dealing desks with prior CBS notification; practical utility is limited because the tala is trade-weighted-basket pegged and the domestic deliverable forward window is operationally narrow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return & Exempt Company License Fee Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour - Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June; initial payment pro-rated from date of incorporation to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 10% of the annual fee per month of delay, up to 50% of the total fee; failure to pay for six consecutive months triggers administrative strike-off of the International Company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a Samoan International Company unless the company is licensed as a bank, insurance carrier, or trust service provider, or unless the shareholders adopt an audit requirement in the Articles of Association; an audit also becomes compulsory if annual subscription revenue exceeds USD 18 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for any voluntarily prepared financial statements; no obligation to file financial statements with the Registrar or any tax authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On every share transfer, the Register of Members must be updated within 14 days; an annual UBO confirmation statement is submitted with the Annual Return, confirming whether any change occurred, with a nil declaration if there have been no changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (IC) on qualifying foreign-source and international-business income; 25% standard corporate rate for resident companies under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2015
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from income tax, stamp duty, estate and transfer duties for ICs transacting with non-residents in the course of international business (International Companies Act 1987, s.6); no capital gains tax; distributions to shareholders are exempt from all Samoan withholding taxes; annual Government Fee and SIFA administrative fee are the sole periodic levies

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return and Economic Substance Return filed through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Registry portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return due on or before each anniversary of incorporation; Economic Substance Return due within 12 months after the close of the IC's accounting period

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and IC registration number as registered with the Registrar of International Companies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the SIFA certificate exactly; non-resident owners should ensure the English name is identical on banking and payment processor records (Stripe, Authorize.Net).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Samoa and licensed registered agent particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Samoan licensed agent is mandatory; the agent files the return on behalf of the non-resident beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors and the company secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: May include non-resident directors; nominee directors must disclose the natural-person principal and written consent must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial shareholders, classes of shares, issued and paid-up capital, and any bearer share status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are subject to mandatory immobilisation; disclose full chain of ownership to the registered agent for AML/beneficial ownership records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Activity Declaration and Economic Substance Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the IC's actual business activity (subscription-box merchandising and logistics) and confirmation of core income-generating activities performed in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A subscription-box business that operates warehouses and fulfillment outside Samoa will normally fail the economic substance declaration; legal advice is required before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Residency and Source of Income Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of foreign-source revenue streams and confirmation that no Samoan-source income was derived
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: ICs are prohibited from trading with Samoan residents; any domestic sales must be disclosed and will trigger income tax obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment of the annual Government Fee attract late-payment surcharges imposed by SIFA; persistent default results in automatic strike-off from the register, restoration costs, and director disqualification; a false economic substance declaration attracts monetary penalties and referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Income Tax Return - Companies (Form IT-CO) via the Ministry for Revenue (MaF) electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Last day of the ninth month following the end of the income year (calendar-year taxpayers: 30 September); different dates apply where MaF has approved a substituted accounting period

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All assessable income derived from Samoan sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue of an IC is exempt; gross income here is WST 0 for a compliant IC with no Samoan-source receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempted under the International Companies Act 1987 and Income Tax Act 2015
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full value of non-resident subscription-box revenue and state the statutory exemption basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses incurred in deriving assessable (Samoan-source) income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally not applicable to fully exempt ICs; deductibility of group allocations is disallowed where no Samoan-source income exists.
WST 0 for an exempt IC; any positive amount is taxed at 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax due at 25% of taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: WST 0 with correct exemption claim; incorrect zero-filing invites audit and 150% evasion penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of tax due for each month or part-month, capped at 25%; unpaid tax interest at 10% per annum; fraudulent failure to file: fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 2015.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% withholding on dividends paid by a Samoan resident company to non-resident shareholders; 0% on distributions made by an International Company to its shareholders by virtue of the IC tax exemption
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's principal double taxation agreement is the Samoa-New Zealand DTA (in force 2012); administrative protocol: (1) the beneficial owner obtains a Tax Residency Certificate from its residence jurisdiction, (2) the paying entity or distribution agent submits a WHT relief application with the TRC to the Ministry for Revenue (MaF), (3) MaF approves a reduced or nil rate before payment is made, and (4) supporting beneficial ownership documentation must be retained for 7 years. An exempt IC is generally not a 'resident' for DTA purposes and will be denied treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, so treaty relief is normally unavailable for IC structures; repatriation is best structured via the 0% IC distribution exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% on gross royalties and 15% on gross interest paid from Samoan sources to non-residents; payments by an IC in connection with its international business are non-Samoan-source and incur 0% Samoan WHT. Under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA, where treaty entitlement is independently established, the maximum rate on interest is 15% and on royalties is 15%; patent and know-how royalties may be apportioned under the DTA's limited force-of-attraction rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File / Master File threshold is expressly prescribed in Samoan Tala (WST); Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015 enforces the arm's length principle and MaF may demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation regardless of transaction size. A prudential compliance threshold for a subscription-box IC is preparation of Master File / Local File documentation where controlled cross-border transactions exceed WST 5,000,000 annually.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies Economic Substance Regulations for International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended 2018) and SIFA Substance Rules. Relevant activities include 'distribution and service centre' business, which captures a subscription-box model involving warehousing, order fulfillment, logistics coordination, and customer service. A compliant IC must (1) perform core income-generating activities in Samoa, (2) maintain adequate physical offices, employees, and expenditure in Samoa, (3) be managed and controlled in Samoa, and (4) file an annual economic substance return. An IC whose subscription-box operations are fully performed abroad fails the substance test, loses the exemption protection, and becomes liable to information exchange and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC derives prohibited Samoan-source revenue (sales to Samoan residents, Samoan fulfillment services, or investment in Samoan assets) and conceals it from the registered agent, the SIFA annual return, and the Ministry for Revenue to preserve the zero-tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of corporate income tax at 25% on concealed income; penalty surcharge of 150% of the tax avoided; interest at 10% per annum; criminal prosecution for tax evasion carrying a fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 2015; possible deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax where the corporate form is used as a sham; the Supreme Court may issue asset restraint orders and travel bans; directors face criminal conviction, disqualification from managing Samoan companies, and civil restitution of diverted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a shell with no physical office, no employees, no board meetings in Samoa, and performing all subscription-box logistics, fulfillment, trading, and management functions abroad while claiming the benefit of Samoa's zero-tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFA monetary penalties for late or false economic substance filings; compulsory exchange of information with foreign tax authorities; automatic revocation of tax-exempt privileges; strike-off from the register with loss of legal capacity; potential inclusion of the entity on international harmful-tax-practices listings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false substance declarations are personally liable for fines and imprisonment; nominee directors face indemnity claims and asset freezes; directors of a struck-off company are jointly liable for the company's unpaid fees and penalties in civil proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify ultimate beneficial owners, concealment of ownership through silent nominees, use of non-compliant bearer-share arrangements, or refusal to respond to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the registered agent's enhanced due diligence requests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and imprisonment under the Samoa Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2007; freezing orders on the IC's bank accounts and payment processor accounts (Stripe, Authorize.Net); revocation of the registered agent's license and deregistration of the IC; administrative penalties applied by SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face individual criminal liability for money laundering and terrorist financing offences with custodial sentences up to 14 years; civil forfeiture of personal assets; travel restriction orders issued on application of the FIU; lifelong prohibition from acting as a director in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing inconsistent annual returns with SIFA and MaF, fabricating invoices and logistics records to support subscription-box revenue, backdating director resolutions, or misrepresenting the locus of economic substance after a tax audit inquiry has commenced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 150% of the undercharged tax plus interest; prosecution for forgery and false statements; cancellation of the IC's registration by the Registrar; withdrawal of tax-exempt status with retroactive assessment at 25%; referral to the Samoan prosecutorial authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution of all penalties and unpaid taxes; criminal conviction leading to imprisonment; extradition risk where conduct involves foreign customers' funds; permanent ban from holding directorships in Samoa and from engaging licensed agents.
